title: JSON protocol drops item hints in both directions
description:
indigo_libs/indigo_json.c writes the property-level "hints" of every def*Vector but no item-level hints, and its parser reads no hints at all, while indigo_xml.c writes and parses hints on both properties and items (indigo_xml.c hints_attribute(), defSwitch line 2136) and indigo_docs/PROTOCOLS.md line 80 says every item may carry hints. JSON clients such as the web control panel therefore never receive item hints: warn_on_set on AGENT_SCHEDULER_TASK_COMMAND RESET_ALL and DELETE_ALL, SERVER RESTART ('Restart INDIGO Server?'), SERVER INSTALL items, MOUNT_ALIGNMENT_RESET and the Astroasis factory resets. Next: add item "hints" to the JSON writer for all vector types and to the JSON parser, a JSON round-trip unit test, and a server acceptance check that the scheduler hints arrive over the network. Owner chose on 2026-11-14 to record this only.

Imported from .factory/findings/active/FND-20261114090521-b043-scheduler-bulk-command-tests-001.json (category: functional, blocking: no).

outcome.summary: Pass. indigo_json.c json_item_hints() (784-821) emits ', "hints": "..."' after label for every def*Vector item form (text, number rw/ro, switch, light, all three BLOB branches), mirroring indigo_xml.c 2135-2178. Escaping matches indigo_json_escape_b (quote, backslash, \n, \r, \t); the private thread-local buffer (2*512+1+16) holds the worst case (12-byte prefix + 2*511 escaped + quote + NUL) so no truncation, and it does not collide with escape buffers 0/1 or the long buffer used by other arguments of the same SPRINTF. Items without hints get an empty string, so their output is byte-identical to master. Parser: the C JSON parser (top_level_handler, indigo_json.c 341-368) only accepts getProperties and newText/Number/SwitchVector client requests, and its only caller is indigo_server_tcp.c; new*Vector carries no hints in XML either, so omitting a parser change is correct. Tests: json_adapter_serializes_item_hints asserts hinted and unhinted items for every type and would fail on master; I decoded its 6 emitted messages with Python json.raw_decode, all valid with the expected item hints. The scheduler check serialises the agent's real AGENT_SCHEDULER_TASK_COMMAND (observer snapshot) through the real JSON device adapter and finds RESET_ALL/DELETE_ALL warn_on_set; it does not cross a TCP/WebSocket connection, but the server uses that same adapter function, so I accept it as a reasonable realisation. Ran make -C indigo_test test-agent-scheduler: 71 run, 71 passed, 0 failed (reset_all_keeps_running_task_and_urgent_order PASS); test_protocol_json all passed. PROTOCOLS.md line 80 and the 'same features as XML 2.0' claim now hold; no doc change needed. Minor, non-blocking: BLOB hints are only asserted for the no-value branch; the escape loop duplicates indigo_json_escape_b (justified by buffer ownership). Out of scope, for the owner: indigo_server/resource/indigo.js changeProperty (339-351) only honours property-level warn_on_change; nothing in indigo.js/components.js reads i

history.text: Reproducing: item hints test against unfixed writer

Reproduction: new unit test json_adapter_serializes_item_hints in indigo_test/unit/test_protocol_json.c FAILED against the unfixed indigo_json.c (defText/Number/Switch/Light/BLOB output had property hints but no item hints). After the fix it passes, and the scheduler integration case reset_all_keeps_running_task_and_urgent_order (extended with a JSON definition check of RESET_ALL/DELETE_ALL warn_on_set) passes. The C JSON parser handles only getProperties/new*Vector requests; there is no def*Vector parsing in C (indigo.js is the JSON client), so no parser change was made.
Running scheduler integration test: make -C indigo_test test-agent-scheduler

checks.name: unit
checks.command: make Makefile.inc && make init && make -j8 -C indigo_libs all && make -j8 -C indigo_drivers/agent_platesolver -f ../../Makefile.drv all && make -j8 -C indigo_drivers/agent_scheduler -f ../../Makefile.drv all && make -j8 -C indigo_drivers/system_alpaca -f ../../Makefile.drv all && make -C indigo_test test-unit
